channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: ECB’s Kazimir: Key for me will be January repricing
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member and Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS), Peter Kazimir, said during the European trading session on Tuesday that the interest rate hike at the policy meeting earlier this month was “unavoidable”.

item.title: USD/IDR: External headwinds keep upside risks – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong reports USD/IDR briefly traded back towards 18,000 as higher Oil prices, elevated US Treasury yields and a firm Dollar weighed on the Indonesian Rupiah. Bank Indonesia has shifted intervention toward NDF and DNDF, seen as more effective and less reserve-intensive.

item.title: Gold bulls seem hesitant as Fed hike bets, higher bond yields and bullish USD cap upside
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) clings to modest recovery gains through the first half of the European session, albeit it lacks follow-through and remains below $4,150.

item.title: Euro softens against Canadian Dollar amid ECB caution, oil strength
item.description: EUR/CAD halts its three-day winning streak, trading around 1.6100 during the European hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold: Downside risks with key supports in focus – OCBC
item.description: Christopher Wong at OCBC notes Gold has extended its decline to a seven-week low, pressured by higher Oil prices, firm US Treasury yields and a stronger Dollar. The break below $4,200 has intensified technical selling, with near-term direction tied to Oil and rates.

item.title: Iran’s Qalibaf: If Iran cannot sell its oil, no one can in the region
item.description: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf says during the European trading session on Tuesday that no one in the region shall sell its oil if Iran cannot sell its oil, according to state media, Reuters report.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Likely revisit five-month high at around 1.4250
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is up 0.12% at around 1.4190 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: USD/JPY: Intervention threat caps upside – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that Japanese Yen strength has persisted as USD/JPY pulled back toward 156.50 on Monday, with policymakers stepping up verbal warnings on currency weakness and signalling readiness to intervene.

item.title: USD Rates: Bill financing costs rise with Fed hikes – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Eugene Leow analyses how rapidly rising US Treasury yields are complicating financing for the US government as the Federal Reserve hikes rates.

item.title: EUR/USD: Lagarde’s dovish tilt weighs on Euro – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING says EUR/USD downside risks have increased after dovish comments from European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde, which widened SOFR-ESTR spreads and tempered expectations for an October ECB hike.

item.title: AUD/USD: RBA hike fails to lift Aussie – MUFG
item.description: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the Australian Dollar has slipped back below 0.7000 against the US Dollar, testing the 200-day moving average near 0.7030.

item.title: US Treasuries: Yields near multi-decade highs – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank analysts describe a renewed selloff in US Treasuries, with the 10-year yield around 5.25%, close to its 2007 peak and highest levels since 2002 if breached.

item.title: USD: Data risks support Dollar gains – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes fading optimism on US–Iran talks and rising Oil prices are reinforcing support for the Dollar, with Brent near $107 and equities at risk from rapidly rising rates. He sees upcoming US consumer confidence and JOLTS data as key for Dollar direction.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD recovery beyond $61.00 faces selling risk
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) registers a modest recovery from the $60.30 area, or the lowest level since August 5, touched earlier this Tuesday, though it lacks follow-through.

item.title: Brent Oil: Higher prices to extend into 2027 – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Henry Allen and Jim Reid highlight that Brent Oil has surged again, with spot prices above $107 per barrel and December 2027 futures at new highs.

item.title: AUD/USD: RBA hike fails to lift Australian Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole reports the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) raised rates to 4.60% as expected, but AUD/USD fell below 0.700 as Governor Michele Bullock revealed policymakers had considered holding rates due to housing and global risks.

item.title: Swiss Franc languishes at 16-month lows despite bright KOF leading Indicators data
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) extends losses for the fifth consecutive day against a firm US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, unfazed by the unexpected improvement in the KOF leading Indicator report seen earlier in the day.

item.title: Swiss Franc: One-off export surge tempers SNB response – Commerzbank
item.description: Michael Pfister at Commerzbank notes that Switzerland’s strong 1.9% quarter-on-quarter growth was driven mainly by net exports, particularly to the Euro area excluding Germany, rather than a broad-based domestic upswing.

item.title: S&P 500: Higher yields pressure equities – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Early Morning Reid notes that rising US yields and Oil prices are weighing on equities. The S&P 500 fell nearly 0.8%, led by larger declines in the Magnificent 7, while defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare posted modest gains.

item.title: US Dollar: Stock-driven flows raise vulnerability – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur highlights that the US current account deficit remains large at about 3% of GDP and increasingly relies on foreign inflows into US stocks rather than bonds.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar holds ground, markets await comments from Fed officials and US data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, September 29:

item.title: Indian Rupee slumps as Trump refutes claims of Iran sanctions relief
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) slides to a fresh two-month low against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with the USD/INR pair jumping to near 96.13. The pair strengthens as the Indian currency underperforms due to fears of persistent energy supply disruption.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines to near 0.5650 despite RBNZ hike bets
item.description: The NZD/USD pair loses momentum to near 0.5655 during the early European trading hour on Tuesday. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) extends its downside to a three-month low against the US Dollar (USD) amid ongoingUS-Iran tensions. Traders will keep an eye on the Fedspeak later on Tuesday.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Likely revisit yearly high at around 101.80
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) outperforms its peers amid firm expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will deliver more interest rate hikes this year. At press time, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, trades 0.1% higher to near 101.25.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA hike reinforces hawkish stance – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s macro strategy team notes that the Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60%, in line with expectations. The RBA signalled that inflation remains too high and left the door open to further tightening if needed.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA’s hawkish hike caps upside – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur reports that the Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 25 bps to 4.6%, the highest level in about 15 years, and struck a notably hawkish tone.

item.title: Australian Dollar dips to fresh lows sub-0.7000 despite hawkish RBA Bullock
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) extends losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, despite the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) interest rate hike and Governor Bullock's comments hinting at further monetary tightening ahead.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Tests nine-day EMA support after falling below 157.50
item.description: USD/JPY loses ground after posting minor gains the previous day, trading around 157.30 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The currency pair is remaining within a symmetrical triangle, which indicates a period of market consolidation, where neither buyers nor sellers are in control.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Fresh downside leg likely below 1.3200
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is down 0.15% at around 1.3234 against the US Dollar (USD) during the early European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Bullock Speech: RBA Governor speaks on policy outlook after the expected interest rate hike
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock is addressing the press conference, explaining the reason behind raising the key interest rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 4.60% from 4.35% in the September policy meeting.
